instruction.what: The evidence validation (B5) of one subgroup, after its sweep, the gate before 3.1: the code checks of its observations (shown in `code_checks`), and the reading of every evidence observation of the subgroup (its own of S1 to 2.1, and the older ones on its occurrences kept as evidence) for whether it is true, founded and coherent with the others. Inner being is not judged here; the two validations are never run together.
read: Read the code checks first: a failing check names observations to repair (unmarked, no node, a word node missing a column without its reason, a trace to a deleted observation, two of one text, a B1 observation no sense traces, a sense the 2.1 observations on its occurrences do not trace, an older observation left open).

Take one observation at a time (`observations`, in the order of the steps): its text, basis and grounds against its verses (`verses`) and the observations it traces. Is it true of those verses? Does it say more than they show? Does it contradict another observation of the subgroup?
write: Fill `answer.observations`, one entry for each observation of the package: verdict true, with `why` (what in the verses and the data bears it out); or verdict repair, with `why` (what is wrong) and `actions`: the actions of the validation that repair it (cfg_setting validate.reading actions, each with its parameters, for example {"action": "restate", "oid": id, "new_text": ..., "checked": ..., "reason": ...}, or delete_neither, complete_node, add_trace).
A repair is checked as it is written; an observation that cannot be made true is deleted with its reason.

Then: Collection-Build.ps1 -Action CheckAnswer -File <the answer file>: every problem at once, each with its rule, nothing written; correct the answer until it finds none, then -Action RecordEvidence -File <the answer file>, and ReadEvidence again until every evidence observation is read; the gate passes when all are read and the code checks pass.

keep.text: A sheet of validation actions is checked whole (every action named, its parameters complete) and written in one transaction: any action the tables refuse refuses the whole sheet and nothing is kept. -Check runs every action and rolls back. Every change is kept in ib_observation_change with its reason (RW-01); nothing is physically deleted.

A finding of the validation is repaired first: a wording that is untrue or stronger than its verse is restated and the restatement checked against the base data; a node missing a column is completed, or the reason the data cannot give it is recorded; a duplicate is consolidated; a node is deleted only when another live node carries its occurrence or it supports no finding of its observation. A finding is left open only when a named collection's validation will touch the observation: the deferral to that collection and the finding are recorded, and the check accepts it as deferred. A finding with no named owner is closed in the validation.

An older observation is deleted as consumed only when live observations carry its meaning: every word occurrence of it is on a live node of a carrier or named as not carried with its reason, the mapping is stated in words (what the old says, which carrier states each part), the traces to it are re-pointed or replaced, and the consumption is kept as `consumed_by`. An observation that holds more than one finding is split first.

An observation that is neither evidence nor inner being contributes nothing to the purposes of the observations (researcher, 2026-11-22): it is commented with its reason and the word occurrences no other live observation holds, then deleted. An observation already marked, or one another observation traces, is not deleted this way.

Evidence states what the data are or show, tied to a verse. Inner being states how something works in the inner being, based on evidence, a building block of the stage 5 claims. The marker (ib_observation.nature) follows the content and purpose of the observation, never its stage (RS-04): an observation of any stage may be inner being when it traces to evidence. One that states both is split. The marker is set when the observation is created, by the item that is answered (cfg_setting layer.reading items.<item>.nature); a finding file never sets it; the validation changes it only where the content shows the item's nature does not hold.

The validation runs in two layers, never concurrently: evidence first, then inner being. The inner-being layer is judged only when the evidence layer passes (every in-scope observation marked, none without a live node, no word node missing a required column without its reason, no live trace to a deleted observation, no two of one meaning). A later evidence change reopens only the inner-being rows it touches. In the build this gate is: step 3.1 does not open before the evidence layer passes, and step 3.3 does not close before both layers pass (cfg_setting layer.reading open_gate and closing_gate).
No observation is changed except by a reading, and every change is recorded with its reason. An observation no longer supported by the verse is soft-deleted, with the reason.
One observation per finding: the same description is never written twice. Applied to another verse, word or scope it gains a node on the existing observation.
Observation text is concise and tied to this verse's content, never a restatement of the word's dictionary sense. A transliteration is never given without its gloss.
Verse references are resolved fresh at write time, never taken from the text written. Relations are recorded only on evidence.
Missing data in the base extract is named as a gap, never substituted from memory or outside knowledge.

A node is on one occurrence (verse_lexical_id) and carries the collection of its surface (a supportive node, the collection of the surface it supports); a node already on the observation for the same occurrence is not written twice, and takes the role. A node with no collection to carry, or on a verse out of scope (B:130), is not written and is listed.

Every live observation marked inner_being holds at least one live traced node on a live observation marked evidence, or on a live inner-being observation that itself traces to evidence (the trace chain of stage 4: a 3.2 behaviour traces the 3.1 elements it gathers, a 3.3 match the 3.1 and 3.2 observations it comes from; at most three links), unless it is recorded self-evidencing: it quotes its verse in full and holds a word node for every word it relies on. A traced node never points at a deleted observation. A trace points first at existing evidence; an evidence observation is created only when none states the fact and it states what the nodes and the quotation do not. An inner-being observation traced to evidence not yet marked is pending, not failed.

A step of the layered reading opens only when the grouping is finished (every surface placed in a subgroup or isolated with its reason, every subgroup holding a surface) and the previous step is closed; with -Subgroup the needs and gates are judged for that subgroup alone (#2538). Step S1 is read after the grouping; step 1.1 needs step S1 closed: every word of the subgroup (surface and lettered Strong's code) answered and validated. Opening derives one ledger row for each aspect the data demands (cfg_setting layer.reading); an aspect the data no longer demands is retired, a new one is added, and a second open changes nothing.

A read or record command names a live collection, a live subgroup of it where the read is by subgroup, and a step or item the layered reading knows. A command that names one that does not exist is refused and writes nothing.

An answer is the output form its read wrote: the `command` of that read; every entry an object, or a list, where the form has one; each field in its place with its type (a key unique in the answer, a text, a reason in words); each item answered once; and at least one entry where the form asks for entries. A file in another shape is refused whole and nothing is written.

Every ledger row, occurrence, observation, sense, node, verse and collection an answer names is one the packet offered for this unit, or a key the answer itself defines, and is live in the database. A name outside them is refused.

Every coded value of an answer (kind, basis, item, part, role, route, mode, polarity, flag type, disposition, verdict, action, nature, stage, status) is one of the values the configuration allows for it (cfg_enum, cfg_setting layer.reading, reading.observation_items, validate.reading), as the packet lists them. Any other value is refused.

A read or record runs only where the ledger has its unit at that step: the row open, or answered and not yet validated, and the steps before it closed (S1 before 1.1; the 2.1 rows before the sweep; the sweep before the evidence validation; its gate before 3.1; every subgroup through 3.1 before 3.2). Out of order it is refused, and the message names what comes first.

A read writes its packet within the time and size the configuration sets (cfg_setting layer.read_types: limits, package_max_chars, read_max_seconds). A read that would exceed them is refused, nothing is written, and the limit is named.

The code of the reading runs only where the configuration it reads is in place (the settings, steps, items, natures, enums and rules it names). Where the code is ahead of the configuration, the command is refused and names what is missing.

Every older live observation with a live node on an occurrence of the row (a stage that is not the build's own) is answered in fill.older when the row is recorded, once: keep or restate (each with its marker), merge into a named observation, consume (live observations carry its meaning, stated in words, verified before it is deleted), delete as neither (comment first), or defer to a named collection (marked now; only the finding is left to that collection). An observation already marked by the validation, answered in a build or deferred is not asked again. A new observation whose text equals that of another live observation of the collection is refused, the other named. LayerCheck re-derives both from the tables. The end state of a collection's build is that every observation of its scope is marked and fixed or deleted, every word node complete or with its reason, and each deferral owned by a named collection.

A lookup of related data in the build or the validation is by an indexed column and takes a chunk of ids (cfg_setting layer.scan chunk); none runs once for each item of a list, and a statement that uses more work than layer.scan max_vm_ops is stopped and named, nothing written (lib/scanguard.py). The tests refuse a statement of the build whose query plan scans a table (layer.scan scan_ok lists the temporary tables a statement may scan).

observations.text: In Jude 7 aperchomai, usually to go away or depart (aorist participle), is rendered 'pursued' with 'unnatural desire' as its object: the cities went off after other flesh, so the going away is a going after a desire.
observations.grounds: pursued unnatural desire

observations.text: In Rom 9:31 dioko (pursue; present participle) has as object a law leading to righteousness, and the verse says Israel did not reach that law: a pursuit toward a goal that is not attained.
observations.grounds: pursued a law that would lead to righteousness

observations.text: In Rev 12:13 dioko (aorist indicative) is the dragon's chase of the woman who bore the male child, after he was thrown down: a hostile pursuit of a person, not of a goal.
observations.grounds: he pursued the woman

observations.text: In Exo 14:8, Jos 8:16, Judg 4:16, 2Sa 2:19 and the other verses of this row, achar (after, behind; a preposition in construct) is the word after the verb of chasing that the ESV folds into 'pursued': it marks the one chased as ahead, and is not the act itself.
observations.grounds: he pursued the people of Israel

observations.text: In Judg 20:45 dabaq, whose sense is to cling or keep close, is a Hiphil rendered 'pursued hard': those who fled were followed close and overtaken, and two thousand of them struck down.
observations.grounds: they were pursued hard to Gidom

observations.text: In Num 14:45 katat, whose sense is to beat or crush, is a Hiphil the ESV renders 'pursued': the Amalekites and Canaanites beat Israel down and drove them as far as Hormah; the English hides the crushing.
observations.grounds: defeated them and pursued them, even to Hormah

observations.text: In Gen 14:15, Exo 14:9, Jos 8:16, Judg 4:16, 1Sa 17:52, 2Sa 2:19, 2Ki 25:5, Psa 18:37 and the other verses of this reading, radaph (pursue; mostly Qal narrative) is chasing a fleeing person or army to overtake, capture or strike it, often with how far the chase ran.
observations.grounds: pursued them to Hobah

observations.text: In Psa 109:16, Psa 143:3, Amo 1:11 and Lam 3:43 radaph is pursuit of the weak to destroy them: the poor and needy to death, the speaker's soul crushed, a brother with the sword with pity cast off, a people killed without pity in anger.
observations.grounds: pursued the poor and needy and the brokenhearted

observations.text: In Job 30:15 radaph is passive (Qal imperfect, feminine) with honor as its subject: Job's honor is chased away as by the wind, beside terrors turned on him and prosperity passed like a cloud.
observations.grounds: my honor is pursued as by the wind

observations.text: In 1Ti 6:11 de (but) is the particle the surface 'Pursue' carries with dioko at the same place: it opens the turn from fleeing these things to pursuing righteousness, and is not itself the act.
observations.grounds: But as for you, O man of God

observations.text: In Rom 14:19, 1Cor 14:1, 1Ti 6:11, 2Ti 2:22 and 1Pe 3:11 dioko (pursue; imperative or hortatory) has a good to be pursued as object: peace and mutual upbuilding, love, righteousness and the virtues listed, peace sought and pursued.
observations.grounds: let us pursue what makes for peace

observations.text: In Rom 9:30 dioko (present participle) is negated: the nations that made no pursuit of righteousness are said to have reached it, a righteousness by faith, so the reaching comes without the pursuit.
observations.grounds: who did not pursue righteousness have attained it

observations.text: In Gen 35:5, Exo 14:4, Deu 19:6, Jos 10:19, 2Sa 17:1, Jer 48:2 and the other verses of this row, achar (after; a preposition in construct) stands with the verb of chasing that the ESV renders 'pursue', marking the one chased as ahead; it is not the act itself.
observations.grounds: he will pursue them

observations.text: In Jer 48:2 halak (go, walk; Qal imperfect, feminine) with achar is rendered 'pursue' and has the sword as its subject: the sword will go after Madmen, a going that is a pursuit to destroy.
observations.grounds: the sword shall pursue you

observations.text: In Exo 14:4, Jos 2:5, Jos 10:19, 1Sa 30:8, 2Sa 20:6, Hos 8:3 and the other verses of this reading, radaph is chasing a person or a band to overtake or strike them: foretold, commanded, asked about, or negated as in Gen 35:5, where terror from God stops it.
observations.grounds: Pursue your enemies; attack their rear guard

observations.text: In Exo 15:9 and Deu 19:6 the verse names what drives the pursuit: in Exo 15:9 the enemy's desire to have its fill of them, in Deu 19:6 the hot anger of the avenger of blood.
observations.grounds: my desire shall have its fill of them

observations.text: In 1Sa 25:29, Psa 7:5, Psa 71:11, Job 19:22 and Job 19:28 radaph is pursuit aimed at a person's life or standing: men seeking David's life, an enemy after the speaker's soul, foes saying God has forsaken him, Job's friends hounding him.
observations.grounds: let the enemy pursue my soul

observations.text: In Psa 83:15, Jer 29:18, Lam 3:66, Nah 1:8 and Job 13:25 God is the one who pursues: with tempest, with sword, famine and pestilence, in anger, into darkness, and in Job's question whether he will pursue dry chaff.
observations.grounds: pursue them with your tempest

observations.text: In Deu 28:22, Deu 28:45 and Eze 35:6 the pursuers are not persons: diseases and blight, the curses for disobedience, and blood for one who did not hate bloodshed pursue and overtake.
observations.grounds: blood shall pursue you

observations.text: In Psa 34:14 and Isa 51:1 radaph has a good as its object: peace to be sought and pursued, and righteousness pursued by those who seek the Lord.
observations.grounds: seek peace and pursue it

observations.text: In Hos 2:7 radaph (Piel) is the unfaithful wife's chase of her lovers, which fails: she will not overtake them or find them, and then turns back to her first husband.
observations.grounds: She shall pursue her lovers but not overtake them

observations.text: Chasing to overtake: running after a person, band or army to overtake, capture or strike them, in Gen 14:15, Exo 14:9, Jos 10:19, Judg 4:16, Judg 20:45, Num 14:45, 1Sa 30:8, 2Sa 2:19, 2Ki 25:5 and the many other battle and flight narratives.
observations.grounds: to pursue, put to flight, chase

observations.text: Hounding to destroy: pursuit aimed at a person's life, standing or the weak, driven in some verses by desire or anger, in Exo 15:9, Deu 19:6, 1Sa 25:29, Psa 7:5, Psa 71:11, Psa 109:16, Psa 143:3, Job 19:22, Amo 1:11, Lam 3:43 and Rev 12:13.
observations.grounds: to persecute, harass (fig)

observations.text: Pursuit by God or by what is not a person: God pursuing with tempest, sword or flood (Psa 83:15, Jer 29:18, Lam 3:66, Nah 1:8, Job 13:25), and curses, diseases, blood and the sword as pursuers (Deu 28:22, Deu 28:45, Eze 35:6, Jer 48:2), with honor chased off in Job 30:15.
observations.grounds: to be behind, follow after, pursue

observations.text: Pursuit of a good: going after righteousness, peace, love and the virtues as an aim, in Rom 9:30, Rom 9:31, Rom 14:19, 1Cor 14:1, 1Ti 6:11, 2Ti 2:22, 1Pe 3:11, Psa 34:14 and Isa 51:1.
observations.grounds: to follow eagerly, endeavor earnestly to acquire

observations.text: Going after a forbidden desire: the cities of Jude 7 going after other flesh, and the wife of Hos 2:7 chasing her lovers without reaching them.
observations.grounds: to go away, withdraw

observations.text: radaph (H7291) is to be behind and follow after, to chase and put to flight; achar (H0310A, after) marks the one chased as ahead; dabaq (H1692) adds keeping close and overtaking in Judg 20:45, and katat (H3807, to crush) in Num 14:45 adds the beating down the ESV renders as pursuit. The lexicon bears out the chase.
observations.grounds: to pursue, put to flight, chase

observations.text: radaph (H7291) has the figurative sense to persecute and harass, and dioko (G1377) the sense to oppress a person or group systematically, the dragon's pursuit in Rev 12:13; al (H5921A, upon) in Amo 1:11 is a preposition and adds no meaning. The lexicon bears out a hostile pursuit.
observations.grounds: to persecute, harass (fig)

observations.text: radaph (H7291) carries no sense of its own for a pursuer that is God, a curse or blood; the lexicon gives the chase, and the verses Psa 83:15, Deu 28:45 and Eze 35:6 supply the pursuer. halak (H1980N) with achar in Jer 48:2 is to go after, given here to the sword.
observations.grounds: to be behind, follow after, pursue

observations.text: dioko (G1377) from the image of the chase has the sense of pressing on to a goal and following eagerly to acquire it, which Rom 14:19 and 1Ti 6:11 use; radaph (H7291) has the figurative sense to follow after and aim to secure, used in Psa 34:14 and Isa 51:1. de (G1161) is a particle and adds no meaning.
observations.grounds: to follow eagerly, endeavor earnestly to acquire

observations.text: aperchomai (G0565) is to go away or depart, and opiso (G3694, after) in Jude 7 turns the going away into a going after; radaph (H7291) in Hos 2:7 is the chase itself. The lexicon has no sense of desire in these codes; the desire is in the objects the verses name.
observations.grounds: to go away, withdraw

observations.text: In Gen 35:5, Exo 14:4, Deu 19:6, Jos 8:16, Jos 10:19, 2Sa 17:1, 2Sa 20:6, 2Sa 20:7 and 2Sa 20:13 the surface pursue stands on two codes at one place, radaph (H7291) and achar (H0310A, after): the verb and the word that marks the one chased as ahead.
observations.grounds: he will pursue them

observations.text: In the other Hebrew verses of the row, among them Exo 15:9, Deu 28:45, Psa 34:14, Lam 3:66, Hos 2:7 and Nah 1:8, the surface pursue stands on radaph (H7291) alone, whether the object is a person, a good or the one God pursues.
observations.grounds: seek peace and pursue it

observations.text: In Jer 48:2 the surface pursue stands on halak (H1980N, go) with achar (H0310A, after), not on radaph: the sword goes after Madmen.
observations.grounds: the sword shall pursue you

observations.text: In Rom 9:30, Rom 14:19, 1Cor 14:1, 1Ti 6:11, 2Ti 2:22 and 1Pe 3:11 the surface pursue stands on dioko (G1377), and in 1Ti 6:11 also on de (G1161, but), the particle at the same place.
observations.grounds: Pursue love, and earnestly desire

observations.text: In Exo 14:8, Exo 14:9, Jos 8:16, Judg 4:16, 2Sa 2:19, 2Ki 9:27, Jer 39:5 and the other verses where both stand, the surface pursued holds radaph (H7291) and achar (H0310A, after) at one place, the verb with the word that sets the one chased ahead.
observations.grounds: he pursued the people of Israel

observations.text: In Amo 1:11 the surface pursued holds radaph (H7291) with al (H5921A, upon), so the brother Edom pursued stands as the one the pursuit comes upon.
observations.grounds: he pursued his brother with the sword

observations.text: In Gen 14:15, Exo 14:23, Jos 8:24, 1Sa 30:10, Psa 18:37, Psa 109:16, Job 30:15 and the other verses of radaph alone, the surface pursued stands on radaph (H7291) with no second code.
observations.grounds: pursued them to Hobah

observations.text: In Num 14:45 the surface pursued stands on katat (H3807, crush) and in Judg 20:45 on dabaq (H1692, keep close): neither is radaph, and the English gives both as pursuit.
observations.grounds: they were pursued hard to Gidom

observations.text: In Rom 9:31 and Rev 12:13 the surface pursued stands on dioko (G1377), and in Jude 7 on aperchomai (G0565, go away) with opiso (G3694, after), a going away after unnatural desire.
observations.grounds: he pursued the woman
